chunks: 2716 - And it is narrated from Khalid, the seller of caps, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who had intercourse with his wife while the ṭawāf al-nisāʾ was still due upon him.

He عليه السلام said: "A camel is due from him." Then another came and asked him about it, so he said: "A cow is due from him." Then another came and asked him about it, so he said: "A sheep is due from him."

So I said after they had stood up: "May Allah set you right, how did you say that a camel was due from him?" He عليه السلام said: "You are wealthy, so a camel is due from you; upon the one of moderate means is a cow; and upon the poor is a sheep."

key_terms.الْفَقِيرِ: one who is poor and of limited means
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: the post-hajj circumambulation whose completion makes marital relations lawful

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for having intercourse before completing ṭawāf al-nisāʾ?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who has intercourse with his wife before completing ṭawāf al-nisāʾ. The expiation varies according to financial capacity: a camel for the wealthy, a cow for one of moderate means, and a sheep for the poor.
